clue.text: Leave behind sailor and almost one boat…

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: almost signals the word one loses its final letter

parts.note: a boat or ship, a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone deserts a sailor and very nearly a single vessel, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ONE to ON. The ellipsis links to the next clue but this clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The order to quit a sinking vessel means leaving the craft behind.

clue.text: One genuflecting in the garden

parts.note: one who kneels or bends the head in homage, read also as a leafy shady arbour found in a garden

explanation.walkthrough: Read as BOW-ER, one who bows, it is a worshipper; read normally it is a shady garden retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour or leafy recess is a garden feature, and one who bows is literally a bow-er.

clue.text: Stormy rain round front of heavenly place

indicators.note: round tells us the rearranged letters go about the next piece
stormy suggests turbulence, so the word rain is thrown into disorder

parts.note: the van is the front of an army or procession, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: Wild rain lashes the approach to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' rearranges RAIN to NIRA, and 'round' puts it about VAN. 'front of' looks like an instruction to take the first letter of 'heavenly', but 'front' gives VAN and 'heavenly place' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of perfect bliss, often spoken of as a paradise.

clue.text: I mixed toddy outside-there's a strange thing

indicators.note: outside tells us the jumbled letters sit around the letter I
mixed implies the drink's letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a hot toddy out of doors and finds something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns TODDY into ODDTY, and 'outside' places those letters around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peculiar or unusual is a curiosity.

clue.text: Pity one can come out in it

definitions.text: one can come out in it
definitions.meaning: workers come out on strike in support of others' cause

explanation.surface: Compassion is something a worker can strike for.
explanation.walkthrough: A sympathy strike is one where workers walk out to support others, so one 'comes out in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion is fellow feeling, and a solidarity strike is called by that name too.

clue.text: In difficulty moving to Spain

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters relocate, so to and Spain are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble decides to relocate to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the seven letters of TO SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a fix or a tight corner is an idiom for trouble.

clue.text: Impossibly professional Scottish footballer gets it before four at the city

indicators.note: before puts the word it ahead of the next piece

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a Hib is a player for Hibernian, the Edinburgh football club known as Hibs
IV is four in Roman numerals
Ely is the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A professional Scottish player arrives somewhere in town before four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: HIB is a player for Hibernian, an Edinburgh club. 'before' sets IT ahead of IV, and ELY is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively, so as to rule something out, as with costs too high to bear.

clue.text: Some radiant husks in the plant

indicators.note: some means only part of the phrase radiant husks is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Bright shells are found on a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters from RADIANT HUSKS.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus of pinks and carnations, a flowering garden plant.

clue.text: Kept aside in the freezer perhaps

definitions.meaning: stored at a low temperature, a freezer being one example

explanation.definitionFit: Shelving a plan is putting it on ice, and chilled food is literally kept in such a store.

clue.text: … disagreeable boatman?

parts.note: someone who pulls oars, punning on a person who quarrels, since a row is also an argument

explanation.walkthrough: A 'row' is a quarrel as well as a stint at the oars, so the disagreeable one and the boatman share a name. The ellipsis joins it to the previous clue's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: One who propels a boat with oars, and by pun one who has rows or arguments.

clue.text: Ruin of mother country

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a country or nation

explanation.surface: A matriarch brings disaster on her homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM is a female parent, used of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal punishment in hell is a ruin of the soul, condemnation.

clue.text: A simple brew

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant, so this is a drink infused from such plants

explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like 'plain' but is an old noun for a medicinal herb.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of leaves or flowers made like tea is a brew of medicinal plants.

clue.text: Peter to appear in a show shortly at Christmas time

definitions.text: a show shortly at Christmas time

parts.note: Peter Pan, J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up
taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter is about to star in a seasonal show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' shortens the name of the show inside the definition. Peter Pan is itself a classic Christmas show in Britain, where pantomimes are family comedies staged in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime, cut short, is the British family comedy staged in the festive season.

clue.text: Does it cut round curves?

parts.note: a tool with a thin blade held in an arched frame, used for curved cuts in wood

explanation.walkthrough: The name sounds like a saw that bends; in fact its frame is bow-shaped and it cuts curves.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw tensioned in a curved frame, suited to shaping curved timber.

clue.text: Bird having frolic in forest first

indicators.note: first says the forest word comes ahead of the frolic word

parts.note: a wood is a forest
a lark is a prank or frolic

explanation.surface: A bird enjoys a romp among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts WOOD ahead of LARK, though the clue names the frolic first.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European songbird of the lark family, found in heaths and open woodland.

clue.text: Roof of yonder church Edward completed

parts.note: yonder means that one over there
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward finishes the roof of the church over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completed' turns the verb 'Roof' into the past form the answer needs, so the definition is really 'Roof ... completed'. CH and ED are standard short forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering a roof with straw or reeds is the traditional cottage method, here in finished form.

clue.text: Volume right to be included then excluded from the computer information

indicators.note: to be included says the right letter goes inside the volume word

parts.note: a pint is a measure of volume
out means left out or excluded

explanation.surface: A book's right to appear is granted and then withdrawn from the computer records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' looks like a book but is a measure, PINT; 'to be included' puts R inside it. 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper output from a computer, a hard copy of the data.

clue.text: Dominant partner's wear

parts.note: the partner in charge of a household is said to wear a certain garment, the legs-covering one

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'wear the trousers' means to be the one in charge in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being boss at home names this legwear.

clue.text: Rent rises during visit to this impressive home

indicators.note: during says the reversed rent word sits in the middle of the visit word

parts.note: a stay is a visit

indicators.note: rises, in a down clue, means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: The rent goes up while you are staying at this grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns LET into TEL, and 'during' sets it inside STAY. The definition 'impressive' goes with 'home', as in a British stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignified and grand in appearance, majestic.

clue.text: Abstainer takes comfort in the service

indicators.note: takes means the abstainer letters hold the comfort word inside them

parts.note: TT, teetotal, marks someone who abstains from alcohol
ease is comfort

explanation.surface: A teetotaller finds solace at the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is teetotal; 'takes' puts EASE inside it. 'service' is a set of crockery, not worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of cups, saucers and pot is a tea service.

clue.text: Show old stroke, the same again inside

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: inside says the same-again letters go within the stroke word

parts.note: a hit is a stroke or blow
ib., short for ibidem, is used in references to mean in the same place again

explanation.surface: Someone shows an old stroke, then repeats it inside.
explanation.walkthrough: IB is the short form of ibidem, used in footnotes to point back to the same source again.
explanation.definitionFit: To display or present for public viewing.

clue.text: One touching gently on the mouth

definitions.meaning: one who kisses, touching softly with the lips
slang for the mouth or face

explanation.definitionFit: Someone giving a peck is literally a kisser, and the word is also slang for the lips or face.

clue.text: Against one taking everyone back to the house

parts.note: v., versus, means against
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: back tells us the word for everyone is read in reverse

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A protester goes against the crowd, taking them all back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALL to LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A large country residence or holiday home.

clue.text: One who is very close to you

definitions.text: One who is very close to you

parts.words: One who is very close to you
parts.note: close read as physically nearby, living next door, rather than emotionally intimate

explanation.walkthrough: 'very close' suggests a dear friend, but the nearness is about where they live.
explanation.definitionFit: The person living next door is near in location, not necessarily in affection.

clue.text: Approve a half-pint for the beast

parts.note: to OK something is to approve it

indicators.note: half signals the first two of the four letters of the word pint

explanation.surface: Someone sanctions half a pint for an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps PI, the first two letters of PINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe-like African mammal of the Congo forests.

clue.text: Light-fingered number in carousel going round

indicators.note: in says the number letter is placed within the rearranged letters
going round, like the ride itself, tells us the letters of carousel spin into a new order

explanation.surface: A pickpocket works the crowd on a merry-go-round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rearranges CAROUSEL to LARCEOUS, and 'in' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Given to theft, thieving, like a pickpocket.

clue.text: Sound report of pot-plant

indicators.note: sound at the start says we need a word that is heard like the next one

parts.note: a bang is a loud report, like a gunshot

explanation.surface: A loud noise is said to have come from a house plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' asks for a word that is said like BANG. 'pot-plant' looks like a houseplant, but it is the plant that gives pot, slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian preparation of hemp leaves, smoked or drunk, a cannabis source.

clue.text: There's no knowing where you'll be going on this tour

definitions.text: There's no knowing where you'll be going on this tour

parts.words: There's no knowing where you'll be going on this tour
parts.note: an excursion whose destination is kept secret from the passengers until arrival

explanation.definitionFit: A coach excursion with an undisclosed destination is a well-known British outing.
